The '''2023–24 Bundesliga''' was the 61st season of the [[Bundesliga]], Germany's premier [[Association football|football]] competition. It began on 18 August 2023 and concluded on 18 May 2024.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dfl.de/de/aktuelles/rahmenterminkalender-saison-2023-24/ |title=Rahmenterminkalender für die Saison 2023/24: Bundesnliga-Auftakt am 18. August 2023 – 2. Bundesliga startet am 28. Juli 2023 |trans-title=Framework schedule for the 2023–24 season: Bundesliga kicks off on 18 August 2023 – 2. Bundesliga starts on 28 July 2023 |website=DFL.de |publisher=[[Deutsche Fußball Liga]] |date=9 December 2022 |access-date=12 March 2023 |language=de |archive-date=15 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240415125602/https://www.dfl.de/de/aktuelles/rahmenterminkalender-saison-2023-24/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="calendar">{{cite web |url=https://media.dfl.de/sites/2/2022/12/Rahmenterminkalender-2023_2024.pdf |title=Rahmenterminkalender 2023/2024 |trans-title=2023–2024 framework schedule |website=DFL.de |publisher=[[Deutsche Fußball Liga]] |date=9 December 2022 |access-date=12 March 2023 |language=de |archive-date=15 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240415125558/https://media.dfl.de/sites/2/2022/12/Rahmenterminkalender-2023_2024.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> The fixtures were announced on 30 June 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kicker.de/bundesliga-spielplan-2023-24-fc-bayern-eroeffnet-in-bremen-957300/artikel|title=Bundesliga-Spielplan 2023/24: FC Bayern eröffnet in Bremen|website=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|date=30 June 2023|access-date=30 June 2023|language=de|archive-date=26 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230726130211/https://www.kicker.de/bundesliga-spielplan-2023-24-fc-bayern-eroeffnet-in-bremen-957300/artikel|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 14 April 2024, [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] were crowned champions for the first time with five matches to spare following a 5–0 win over [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]], becoming the thirteenth different champion in Bundesliga history and ending previous holders [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]]'s run of eleven consecutive titles.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bayer Leverkusen beat Werder Bremen to win the Bundesliga!|url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/bayer-leverkusen-werder-bremen-xabi-alonso-champions-title-free-highlights-26914|date=14 April 2024|publisher=Bundesliga|access-date=14 April 2024|archive-date=14 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240414221954/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/bayer-leverkusen-werder-bremen-xabi-alonso-champions-title-free-highlights-26914|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2024/apr/14/bayer-leverkusen-clinch-historic-bundesliga-title-with-rout-of-werder-bremen|title=Bayer Leverkusen clinch historic Bundesliga title with rout of Werder|date=14 April 2024|work=The Guardian|access-date=17 April 2024}}</ref> 

Bayer Leverkusen became the first Bundesliga team to finish an entire season [[List of unbeaten football club seasons|unbeaten]], with a record of 28 wins and six draws.<ref>{{cite news|title=Legendary Bayer Leverkusen complete invincible Bundesliga season|url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/bayern-leverkusen-augsburg-preview-live-blog-report-xabi-alonso-wirtz-unbeaten-27365|date=18 May 2024|publisher=Bundesliga|access-date=18 May 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/article/2024/may/18/european-football-bayer-leverkusen-complete-unbeaten-bundesliga-season|title=European football: Bayer Leverkusen complete unbeaten Bundesliga season|date=18 May 2024|work=Guardian|accessdate=22 May 2024}}</ref>

SV Darmstadt 98 returned to the Bundesliga after a six-year absence<ref>{{Cite web |title=Welcome back to the Bundesliga, Darmstadt! |url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/welcome-back-to-the-bundesliga-darmstadt-klopp-lieberknecht-23547 |access-date=20 May 2023 |website=bundesliga.com |archive-date=20 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230520023059/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/welcome-back-to-the-bundesliga-darmstadt-klopp-lieberknecht-23547 |url-status=live }}</ref> while 1. FC Heidenheim competed in the Bundesliga for the first time in the club's history became 57th Bundesliga club.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Who are Heidenheim, the Frank Schmidt-led club who have defied the odds to make it to the Bundesliga? |url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/who-are-heidenheim-promotion-frank-schmidt-11872 |access-date=2023-05-31 |website=bundesliga.com – the official Bundesliga website |language=en |archive-date=7 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230607203724/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/who-are-heidenheim-promotion-frank-schmidt-11872 |url-status=live }}</ref>
